From 44de8996ed5a10f08f2fe947182da6535edcfae5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sam Edwards <cfsworks@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Dec 2023 19:10:19 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: rockchip: Fix rk3588 USB power-domain clocks

The QoS blocks saved/restored when toggling the PD_USB power domain are
clocked by ACLK_USB. Attempting to access these memory regions without
that clock running will result in an indefinite CPU stall.

The PD_USB node wasn't specifying this clock dependency, resulting in
hangs when trying to toggle the power domain (either on or off), unless
we get "lucky" and have ACLK_USB running for another reason at the time.
This "luck" can result from the bootloader leaving USB powered/clocked,
and if no built-in driver wants USB, Linux will disable the unused
PD+CLK on boot when {pd,clk}_ignore_unused aren't given. This can also
be unlucky because the two cleanup tasks run in parallel and race: if
the CLK is disabled first, the PD deactivation stalls the boot. In any
case, the PD cannot then be reenabled (if e.g. the driver loads later)
once the clock has been stopped.

Fix this by specifying a dependency on ACLK_USB, instead of only
ACLK_USB_ROOT. The child-parent relationship means the former implies
the latter anyway.

Fixes: c9211fa2602b8 ("arm64: dts: rockchip: Add base DT for rk3588 SoC")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Sam Edwards <CFSworks@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231216021019.1543811-1-CFSworks@gmail.com
[changed to only include the missing clock, not dropping the root-clocks]
Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3588s.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3588s.dtsi
index 457cc1b70dc1..3689cec7a3d5 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3588s.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3588s.dtsi
@@ -1031,6 +1031,7 @@ power-domain@RK3588_PD_USB {
 				reg = <RK3588_PD_USB>;
 				clocks = <&cru PCLK_PHP_ROOT>,
 					 <&cru ACLK_USB_ROOT>,
+					 <&cru ACLK_USB>,
 					 <&cru HCLK_USB_ROOT>,
 					 <&cru HCLK_HOST0>,
 					 <&cru HCLK_HOST_ARB0>,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk3588s.dtsi`**
   - A new clock dependency has been added to the `PD_USB` power domain node. Specifically, the line `clocks = <&cru PCLK_PHP_ROOT>, <&cru ACLK_USB_ROOT>, <&cru ACLK_USB>, <&cru HCLK_USB_ROOT>, <&cru HCLK_HOST0>, <&cru HCLK_HOST_ARB0>,` was modified to include `<&cru ACLK_USB>`. This change ensures that the `PD_USB` power domain correctly specifies its dependency on the `ACLK_USB` clock.

### Relationships

- The modification establishes a direct relationship between the `PD_USB` power domain and the `ACLK_USB` clock. By specifying this dependency, the patch addresses the issue of CPU stalls that occur when the power domain is toggled without the necessary clock being active. This change is crucial for ensuring that the QoS blocks are properly managed, preventing hangs during power domain transitions. The relationship implies that the `PD_USB` cannot function correctly without the `ACLK_USB` clock being enabled, thus enhancing the stability of the system when managing USB power domains.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `PD_USB` power domain not specifying a dependency on the `ACLK_USB` clock. This oversight meant that when the power domain was toggled, it could lead to situations where the necessary clock was not running, resulting in indefinite CPU stalls when accessing memory regions associated with the QoS blocks. The lack of this clock dependency could lead to race conditions during system initialization, where the clock might be disabled before the power domain is deactivated, causing hangs and preventing re-enabling of the power domain later.
